title: EHR Consultation Workflow: Guided Simulation
subtitle: Guided practice on a test patient
notes: Companion: Dr. Omar, char-omar-welcome, L1 half-body bottom-right (alt: Dr. Omar, the family physician, welcoming the learner.). Speaker: Dr. Omar. Brand D11 draft in use.
narration_text: Dr. Omar: Welcome to EHR Consultation Workflow: Guided Simulation. You will practise decisions that help you act with confidence. You will leave with practical actions for your next shift.

title: Why + disclaimer
body_html:
Complete, specific, linked — on the day

  • Complete: every mandatory section is filled in before you finish.
  • Specific: a precise primary diagnosis, searched by ICD-10 code or name.
  • Linked: each order points to the diagnosis you assessed.
  • On the day: the record is completed during the consultation day.

Everything here is a test patient. All names, numbers and records are fictional.

Clinical examples show how to use the system. They are not treatment guidance. ⚠ Draft — pending B7

The clinic EHR (product name and version ⚠ Draft — pending B3).
notes: Companion: Dr. Omar, char-omar-explaining, L3 right column (alt: Dr. Omar, the family physician, explaining.). Speaker: Dr. Omar. Draft decisions shown on screen: B7 disclaimer wording (decision-sheet recommended wording), B3 product name ('the clinic EHR'). The ehr-capture-sheet diagram listed on the card is a production checklist; it is not placed so the companion keeps the L3 media column.
narration_text: Dr. Omar: Complete, specific, linked — on the day. Read the disclaimer.

title: Why it won't complete
prompt_html: You press Complete and the system refuses. The form shows chief complaint, HPI and examination filled in. What is the most likely cause?

options.text_html: The plan of care (a mandatory section) is still empty.
options.feedback_html: Yes. The consultation cannot be completed while a mandatory section, such as the plan of care, is empty. Mandatory-field list ⚠ Draft — pending B4.

options.text_html: The consultation summary has not been printed yet.
options.feedback_html: Printing the summary is a separate step. It does not block completion; an empty mandatory section does.

options.text_html: The chief complaint is too short.
options.feedback_html: A short chief complaint is still filled in. The system blocks completion when a mandatory section is empty.

options.text_html: The test patient record is read-only.
options.feedback_html: The record accepted your other entries, so it is not read-only. Look for a mandatory section that is still empty.

feedback.correct_html: Correct. Chief complaint, HPI and examination are done, but the plan of care is empty. Fill every mandatory section, then complete. ⚠ Draft — pending B4.
feedback.incorrect_html: Compare the filled sections with the mandatory list on the previous screen. Which one is missing?

notes: B4 open: the correct answer uses the draft mandatory list (plan of care). Marked '⚠ Draft — pending B4' in feedback.

title: Non-formulary
prompt_html: You order Medicine B, a non-formulary item (example ⚠ Draft — pending B6). The system flags it. What does that mean?

options.text_html: It needs approval before it can be dispensed; consider a formulary alternative.
options.feedback_html: Yes. A non-formulary item needs approval first, so a formulary alternative may be quicker for the patient.

options.text_html: The order has been cancelled automatically.
options.feedback_html: The flag does not cancel the order. It tells you the item needs approval before it can be dispensed.

options.text_html: The dose is wrong and must be changed.
options.feedback_html: The flag is about the item's formulary status, not the dose.

options.text_html: Nothing; the flag is for information only and can be ignored.
options.feedback_html: Ignoring it delays the patient: the item can't be dispensed until it is approved.

feedback.correct_html: Correct. Non-formulary means approval before dispensing. Consider a formulary alternative. Which item needs approval ⚠ Draft — pending B6.
feedback.incorrect_html: Think about what the formulary is: the list of items that can be dispensed without extra approval.

notes: B6 open: 'Medicine B' is a neutral placeholder for the Pharmacy-confirmed non-formulary item.
narration_text: Dr. Omar: Decide as you would on shift, then read the feedback.

title: Why link to a diagnosis
prompt_html: Why must each order be linked to the assessed diagnosis?

options.text_html: It shows medical necessity to the reviewer and keeps the record consistent.
options.feedback_html: Yes. The link explains why the order was needed. Unlinked orders are a common rejection cause (module 05).

options.text_html: So the order appears on the printed summary.
options.feedback_html: Orders appear on the summary either way. The link is about medical necessity and a consistent record.

options.text_html: It is optional; it only helps internal reporting.
options.feedback_html: It is not optional in practice: unlinked orders are a common cause of claim rejections.

options.text_html: So the pharmacy can see the price of the item.
options.feedback_html: The diagnosis link does not show prices. It tells the reviewer why the order was needed.

feedback.correct_html: Correct. A linked order shows medical necessity and keeps the record consistent; unlinked orders are a common rejection cause. See module 05.
feedback.incorrect_html: Think about the reviewer who reads the claim: what tells them why each order was needed?

notes: Links to module 05 (RCM documentation and coding).

title: The whole workflow
prompt_html: Put the nine consultation steps in the correct order.

feedback.correct_html: Correct. Open → Document → Diagnose → Order → Review orders → Summary → Educate → Refer & follow up → Complete. Each step uses what the step before it recorded.
feedback.incorrect_html: Start from opening the consultation and end with completing it. The diagnosis comes before the orders that link to it.

narration_text: Dr. Omar: Put the steps in the order you would follow at work, then read the feedback.

title: Complete the encounter
body_html:
Complete the encounter

  1. Save: wait for “Record saved successfully”.
  2. Press Complete.

If a field is missing

The system will not complete the consultation. Go back to the empty mandatory section, fill it in, save, then complete. Mandatory-field list ⚠ Draft — pending B4.

Where to get help

Contact the IT service desk. Contact details ⚠ Draft — pending B3/B5.
notes: B4 mandatory list and IT service-desk contact details are open; confirm button labels (B5).
